date_note: SecurityWeek, relaying the company update, gives 20 November as the day the systems were impacted.
exec: Peninsula Energy says operations at its Lance uranium project are suspended after its plant and wellfield operating and control systems were impacted; it says corporate and administrative systems remain unaffected, per SecurityWeek.
geo_basis: state named in the source; map pin at the centre of Wyoming
plain: Peninsula Energy says plant and wellfield operating and control systems at its Lance uranium project in Wyoming were impacted on 20 November, and that operations are suspended until recovery and verification are complete, per SecurityWeek.
summary: Cowboy State Daily reports Peninsula Energy told the ASX that a Friday incident breached the operating system at its Lance uranium project in Wyoming, and that administrative systems in the US and Australia were not affected. SecurityWeek reports the company said in a 25 November update that plant and wellfield operating and control systems were impacted on 20 November and operations are suspended until a recovery and verification program is completed.
title: Peninsula Energy says cyberattack hit operating system at Lance uranium project in Wyoming

validation.note: Cowboy State Daily (ASX trading-halt filing) and SecurityWeek (company update of 25 November) are independent publishers that state the incident at the Lance operating systems; The Northern Miner was paywalled after its first paragraph and the ASX announcement itself was not read.

review.note: stronger than the source / source not read: 'operating server' not in Cowboy State Daily or SecurityWeek, Northern Miner paywalled; now 'operating system'; date set to 20 Nov per SecurityWeek; validation note fixed
